findings.source_passage: in short, as a general lassitude overtakes the sated Turk; then a love of ease and virtue supplants the love for maidens; our Ottoman enters upon the impotent, repentant, admonitory stage of life
findings.why_it_matters: The full rhetorical cadence—'impotent, repentant, admonitory stage of life'—is the comic climax of the Ottoman conceit; 'impotent' and 'admonitory' together are the joke. The draft omits 'impotent, repentant, admonitory stage of life' entirely, flattening the satirical sting.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'enters upon the impotent, repentant, admonitory stage of life' verbatim in the passage about the aging schoolmaster whale.

findings.source_passage: like venerable moss-bearded Daniel Boone, he will have no one near him but Nature herself; and her he takes to wife in the wilderness of waters, and the best of wives she is, though she keeps so many moody secrets.
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'The same secludedness and isolation'
findings.why_it_matters: The closing clause—'the best of wives she is, though she keeps so many moody secrets'—is the interpretive and tonal key to the passage, linking Nature's inscrutability to the whale's solitude. The draft cuts it entirely, losing the reflective register.
findings.suggested_fix: Append 'the best of wives she is, though she keeps so many moody secrets' after the Daniel Boone reference.

findings.source_passage: not to exceed half a dozen yards round the waist. Nevertheless, it cannot be denied, that upon the whole they are hereditarily entitled to _en bon point_.
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'The contrast between this Ottoman'
findings.why_it_matters: The setup joke—'not to exceed half a dozen yards round the waist'—is Melville's mock-gallant voice at its most characteristic; dropping the measurement strips the irony from 'en bon point.' The draft gives the conclusion without the absurdist quantification that makes it funny.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-insert 'not to exceed half a dozen yards round the waist' immediately before 'hereditarily entitled to en bon point.'

findings.source_passage: no prudent underwriter would insure them any more than he would a riotous lad at Yale or Harvard
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'The Forty-barrel-bull schools are larger'
findings.why_it_matters: The Yale/Harvard simile is a period-register marker and a comic aside that grounds the schoolboy analogy in social comedy; its omission slightly flattens the satirical texture of the forty-barrel-bull description.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'no prudent underwriter would insure them any more than he would a riotous lad at Yale or Harvard' after the rollicking-rate clause.

summary: Three medium-severity voice flattenings—loss of 'impotent, repentant, admonitory stage of life,' loss of 'moody secrets,' and loss of the waist-measurement joke—collectively strip the chapter's sustained comic-Ottoman conceit of its most characteristic Melvillean inflections, triggering regeneration.
